sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section introduces the patient's complex presentation, emphasizing the triad of fever, neurological symptoms (headache, hiccups), and mucocutaneous lesions. It details the initial confusion regarding the etiology of hyponatremia and CNS inflammation, guiding the reader through the critical first steps of recognizing Behçet's disease (BD) amidst a broad differential of infections and malignancies.
subtopics: Patient demographics and chief complaints: Fever, headache, persistent hiccups, and arthralgia
Mucocutaneous findings: Oral aphthae, folliculitis-like rashes, and genital ulcers
The significance of persistent hiccups as a marker for severe hyponatremia
Initial assessment of volume status: Identifying euvolemia in the presence of hyponatremia
Formulating the initial differential diagnosis: Infectious vs. Neoplastic vs. Autoimmune

sections.section_title: Pathophysiological Basis: Behçet's Disease and Neuro-Inflammation
sections.description: A focused review of Behçet's disease epidemiology and pathology specifically relevant to this case. It explains why concurrent diagnosis is rare, defines acute neuro-Behçet's disease (meningoencephalitis vs. parenchymal lesions), and establishes the theoretical framework for how CNS inflammation can trigger Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH) via cytokine pathways like IL-6.
subtopics: Overview of Behçet's disease: Recurrent oral/genital ulcers, uveitis, and skin lesions
Neuro-Behçet's disease spectrum: Timing of onset (concurrent vs. delayed) and typical brainstem involvement
Mechanisms linking CNS inflammation to SIADH: The role of Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and monocyte activation
Why normal MRI does not rule out acute neuro-BD in early stages

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Confirming SIADH and Excluding Mimics
sections.description: This section walks through the step-by-step logic used to confirm SIADH using strict biochemical criteria (serum/urine osmolality, sodium handling) while systematically ruling out alternative causes such as adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, infection (viral/bacterial/tuberculous), malignancy (lymphoma), and sarcoidosis based on specific negative test results.
subtopics: Applying diagnostic criteria for SIADH: Low serum osmolality with inappropriately high urine osmolality/sodium
Exclusionary workup for endocrine causes: Normal cortisol and thyroid function tests
Infectious workup interpretation: Negative CSF cultures for bacteria/viruses/meningitis pathogens
Differentiating from CNS malignancy: Interpreting elevated sIL-2R in an inflammatory context versus lymphoma
Establishing definite Behçet's disease using International Criteria scoring (oral + genital + skin lesions)

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy: Colchicine Monotherapy in Acute Neuro-BD
sections.description: An exploration of the management decision-making process where colchicine was chosen over standard corticosteroid therapy. It contrasts this approach with conventional guidelines for neuro-BD, discusses the mechanism of action of colchicine against neuro-inflammation, and outlines conservative management strategies for SIADH (fluid restriction).
